newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 17.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet decided yesterday that citizens whose property was destroyed in the floods can obtain up to one million crowns from the state. These households will be able to receive 150,000 and borrow 850,000 crowns.

- The European Commission of the EU yesterday announced a favourable evaluation of the Czech Republic, which should enable the EU to begin talks with Prague over the Czech Republic's future membership.
- The crown dropped yesterday to a record minimum against the U.S. dollar -- 34.30 crowns per dollar. It was 19.065 against the mark.

- The investment company WoodCommerz predicts that damages and economic losses due to massive floods in the east of the country will have a neutral or only slightly negative effect on GDP, which should not decrease by more than one percent from its original estimate of two percent.
- The State Veterinary Administration said that by July 15, more than 135,000 animals were killed by the floods.

PRAVO - Meteorologists expect strong rains at the end of this week, which could increase the level of already high rivers and cause another wave of floods, according to the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute.
- Cabinet Vice-chairman Jiri Skalicky was authorised by the cabinet yesterday to resolve the catastrophic situation. He will organise help and repairs with a team of deputy ministers.
- The Transport Ministry said damages to railway and highway networks amount to 3.6 billion crowns.
- Polls from IVVM show that the opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD) is supported by 28 percent of Czechs, the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) by 20 percent.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The cabinet approved a transport strategy and instructed Transport Minister Martin Riman to add three things to it -- concrete railway reforms, a concept to support public passenger transport unitl 2000 and a proposal for developing transport infrastructure with measures to cut state expenses.

- According to Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl, floods in Moravia and eastern Bohemia caused at least 20 billion crowns damage to industry -- in energy about one billion and in construction and trade several hundreds of millions.
- The Czech National Bank decreased its two-week repo rate yesterday by 0.2 percentage points to 16 percent.
- From today bank IPB will decrease some of its interest rates by between 0.3 and 1.5 percent.

- In May, when the import deposit system was in effect for the first time for a full month, imports from Germany decreased by more than 10 percent, from Slovakia by 13 percent, from Austria by 21 percent and from Italy by 11.3 percent. According to the WTO, of the five largest importers, only Russia had an increase.

- According to the latest survey from GfK, Kraft Jacobs Suchard currently controls 20.6 percent of the domestic coffee market, followed by Douwe Egberts with 20.4 percent and Tchibo with 19.7 percent.
- Plzensky Prazdroj began making its 12-percent light beer Gambrinus in the Lithuanian brewery Ragutis yesterday. Output from Ragutis this year should be 15,000 hectolitres.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The general director of Poldi Steel, Ladislav Gerle, confirmed yesterday that the company should begin manufacturing again in September. It has already received orders.
- Shareholders of Prvni Mestska Banka yesterday approved an increase in basic capital to 1.224 billion crowns from 612 million.

- Yesterday, the cabinet approved a proposal to change the statutes of the Council for Dialogue of Social Partners. It appointed Agriculture Minister Josef Lux and Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl as members of the council.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
